newsitem.title: UK: UK cable industry attacks BSkyB rate card.
newsitem.headline: UK cable industry attacks BSkyB rate card.

text.p: Britain's cable operators said on Wednesday that satellite broadcaster BSkyB's proposed "rate card" would undermine consumer choice in both choice of service and choice of delivery system.
The "rate card" sets out the structure and price which BSkyB charges cable operators for its channels.

In a submission to Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT), the Cable Communications Association (CCA) called for a "fair and reasonable framework" in which BSkyB can flourish, the cable industry develop and in which consumers are free to select services of their choice.

The CCA said the proposed rate card was likely to impede the entry of alternative channels and programme providers into the UK Pay TV market and require a majority of Pay TV consumers to pay for BSkyB whether or not they wanted them.
It said the card could inhibit the development of multi-channel TV in the UK if the cable industry is limited in its ability to offer a viable alternative to Direct-to-Home satellite broadcasting.
"We believe the proposed rate card unfairly discriminates against both cable operators and their customers in favour of Direct-to-Home satellite broadcasting," CCA chairman Stephen Davidson said.
"We want to negotiate with BSkyB to ensure their services are delivered to an ever-wider audience, thereby broadening the base of multi-channel television for the benefit of all," he added.
"Those negotiations must take place within a fair and reasonable framework which accords with the wider consumer interest of competition and choice."
